## Verdict

missing

## Bearer

ProfileSyncListenerService — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/sync/ProfileSyncListenerService.kt

## Trigger

The service being destroyed (`onDestroy`) — nothing observes it, no override exists

## Today

`ProfileSyncListenerService` builds `serviceScope = CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.IO)`
at line 36 and launches into it from `onMessageReceived`. The class overrides
no `onDestroy`, so nothing ever calls `serviceScope.cancel()`; the scope, and
any coroutine launched into it, outlives the service instance and stops only
when the system kills the process.

The identical pattern exists independently in
`RecordedRaceListenerService` — app-phone/src/main/java/com/mgilli/hyroxtracker/sync/RecordedRaceListenerService.kt,
line 32 — which also builds its own `serviceScope` and also overrides no
`onDestroy`. This is a second, independent bearer: the fix in one class does
not reach the other, since neither symbol follows from the other and each
must cancel its own scope.

## Expected

`ProfileSyncListenerService` overrides `onDestroy()`, calls
`serviceScope.cancel()` there, then `super.onDestroy()` — the same pattern
already used for cleanup in `MainActivity.onDestroy()` on both apps (e.g.
app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/MainActivity.kt:124,
app-phone/src/main/java/com/mgilli/hyroxtracker/MainActivity.kt:81).

Second gap: `RecordedRaceListenerService` needs the identical fix —
an `onDestroy()` override cancelling its own `serviceScope` before calling
`super.onDestroy()` — since it is a distinct symbol that does not inherit
the first class's fix.
